decisions.reason: Core glass-silicon via technology aligns with the firm's packaging direction and benefits from established capabilities, so the option remains worth keeping while uncertainty lasts.
Carrier wafers are inexpensive to keep and fit the firm's reusable-carrier focus, preserving a low-cost option without tying up many resources.
The copper interposer is a flagship product central to the multifunctional packaging direction, so management is likely to continue investing despite unresolved demand.
The off-the-shelf brand is close to existing operations, has low carrying cost, and provides a broader market option without large additional commitment.
Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the firm's established glass-wafer capabilities and likely consume resources that could be better used for more promising options.
